headline_marked: [[Truth Social to sell API access]] for real-time posts from top accounts
headline: Truth Social to sell API access for real-time posts from top accounts
summary: Truth Social's new API, launching August 1, will provide businesses with real-time access to posts from its highest-ranking accounts. This move aims to monetize the platform's influence, particularly from President Trump's market-moving updates.
details: Trump Media and Technology Group (TMTG), the company behind Truth Social, announced it will sell access to posts through a new API. Starting August 1, the 'Truth API' will provide businesses with real-time access to content from the platform's highest-ranking accounts.
The API uses industry-standard delivery methods for millisecond access and is expected to offer continuous 24/7 coverage. It will also include a historical archive of posts dating back to 2022.

Unlike some social media sites that previously offered free API access, TMTG CEO Kevin McGurn noted that 'markets already move on Truth Social posts.' This highlights the commercial strategy behind the paid service.

President Trump is a major factor, being the platform's majority shareholder and most followed user with 12.9 million followers. He frequently uses Truth Social to announce significant policies and actions before official channels.
TMTG anticipates the API will be a 'meaningful, ongoing source of revenue' for the company and its shareholders, including the President's family. This strategy aims to create lasting value.

headline_marked: [[Gboard could translate sign language]] into text, beta code reveals
headline: Gboard could translate sign language into text, beta code reveals
summary: A new feature found in Gboard's beta code suggests Google is developing sign-to-text translation, aiming to enhance accessibility for Android users. This AI-powered tool would convert signed gestures into written messages.
details: Google is exploring a new input method for Gboard, allowing users to communicate via sign language directly on their Android phones. This feature would convert signed gestures into text, significantly enhancing accessibility.

The 'Sign-to-text' feature was uncovered by Android Authority, who delved into the beta version of the Gboard app's code. Although the outlet couldn't activate the feature, they found interface images hinting at its functionality.

When enabled, the feature would prompt users to sign to their phone, with AI processing the gestures into text. Google includes a disclaimer, noting that the video itself remains on the device, but data points for sign language analysis are sent to the cloud for processing.

While this advancement promises huge accessibility benefits, the question of language support remains. Given the diversity of sign languages globally, the feature might initially launch in specific regions.

As this is currently only a discovery within beta code, there's a possibility Google could shelve the feature before a public release. Users will need to await further updates to see if it progresses towards a wider rollout.
